PlanningNotes.Note: This plan implements sibling spec.xml, approved explicitly by the user on 2026-09-11. The user also authorized a later implementation commit. This completed plan remains draft until explicitly approved; the recommended execution mode is sequential in the current primary session.

Preflight evidence: grace lint --path . --assertions current reports zero errors and warnings; the baseline leaf suite has 92 passing tests across five existing files, and bun run typecheck passes. Persistence tests currently live inside src/plugins/workflow.test.ts; the separately listed persistence.test.ts target will be newly created, not assumed to exist.

The installed GRACE 4.0.7 module-navigation/module-health assertion error remains a pre-existing blocker requiring resolution or explicit user disposition before execution. Do not change archived assertions or replace the installed CLI within this plan. Approval of this plan alone must not be interpreted as silently waiving that diagnostic.

Before observed implementation writes, run grace lint --path . --change C-DELEGATED-WORKFLOW-ASTRA-PRESETS --assertions baseline --run-commands. After observed and durable changes, run the selected target assertion check externally and the final assertion gate with --run-commands. The target check need not duplicate the final command run. No GRACE lifecycle command is nested in a MustPassCommand.

Baselines inspect behavior-sensitive mode vocabularies, reviewer/close behavior, schema exclusions, parser contracts, and model aliases. Existing documents are not protected only by existence assertions. Target commands additionally verify behavior and new test-file existence prevents Bun silently skipping a misspelled new test path.

Preserve the existing two work-item modes; add mode delegated with an explicitly empty requiredReviewers array and a new awaiting_acceptance state. Missing reviewers never opt into delegated mode. Standalone bounded delegated tasks remain possible without requiring a plan package for every small task.

Managed delegated plans use a separate DelegatedPlanRun registry inside the same session store. The registry owns task-to-work-item mappings, declared checkpoint definitions, review-generation links, historical results, and current completion evidence. Independent review launches reuse ordinary review_only work items, so their existing FAIL-as-findings semantics remain intact.

Add two public tools, work_item_decide and work_checkpoint. work_item_decide accepts workItemId, attempt, decision accept or request_changes, rationale, evidence references, and an explicit concernsDisposition for DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. A separate rework action on the same tool handles later checkpoint findings without overwriting the original acceptance event.

Advertise the two new control tools and delegated-specific open arguments only under the delegated startup profile. Other profiles keep their current tool-schema footprint and policies. Refuse delegated control mutation outside that profile rather than silently switching policy; changing profile still requires restart.

Rework requires a failed checkpoint from the same registered run that covers the accepted task and current accepted attempt. It can reopen that delegated item, including an individually closed item while its plan is still unfinished, without resetting the two-attempt budget. Preserve the historical acceptance, revoke only its current applicability, reject duplicate rework and exhausted budgets, and never reopen blocked/needs_context items or completed plan runs.

work_checkpoint has register, start, and verify actions. Register takes an approved active vvoc planPath, reads and validates the linked approved spec and plan, binds their content hashes and canonical workspace root, and atomically creates the run, its delegated task records, and checkpoint declarations. It does not dispatch agents or execute verification commands. Re-registering identical inputs is idempotent; changed approved inputs are explicit plan drift, not permission to reset an existing run.

Start takes runId and checkpointId, verifies prerequisite acceptance and the declared wave boundary, captures the current scope fingerprint plus accepted task attempts, and opens exactly the declared review_only reviewer set. Verify consumes recorded reviewer results, recomputes the fingerprint and approval-input hashes, and derives passed, failed, stale, or stopped status. An explicit complete: true request is permitted only for the final checkpoint and seals the run only after all current completion conditions pass. Callers cannot submit a boolean declaring a checkpoint passed.

Plan registration derives obligations from the validated file, not a model-supplied list that could omit a checkpoint. Starting dependent-wave tasks is refused while an earlier declared checkpoint barrier is unsatisfied. The final verification result is complete only when all declared tasks are accepted, all prior milestone barriers passed, and the final checkpoint covers current task attempts and the complete declared write scope.

Implementation attempts are bound to the host tool.execute.before/after callID. The model-visible result header remains unchanged. Refuse duplicate in-flight launches and stale result callbacks, consume at most two implementation attempts, and bind decisions to the completed attempt. Format-only repair stays inside its original attempt and receives no new control tools.

New control operations require context.agent equal to vv-controller and a matching root Session response with no parentID. Use pinned SDK ToolContext and PluginInput directory/worktree fields, not an agent name or root path provided in tool arguments. Missing or failing session-identity evidence denies new control mutations. Existing mode behavior is preserved.

Use explicit normalized workspace-relative file lists for task write scopes and checkpoint scopes in this version, not new runtime glob syntax. Reject absolute paths, traversal, wildcard paths, duplicate aliases, symlinks or symlink ancestors, non-regular existing entries, and paths outside the trusted workspace. Missing files are represented explicitly so creations and deletions change the fingerprint.

captureWorkflowSnapshot uses Node SHA-256 over canonical ordered paths, existence markers, file bytes, relevant file-mode metadata, and covered accepted attempt identities. Stream file contents; do not execute commands, copy entire repositories, or add worktrees. Check at checkpoint start, reviewer launch/result boundaries, and final verification. This detects observed snapshot drift; it is not a filesystem lock against arbitrary external writers.

Reject declared delegated writes that overlap an in-flight checkpoint scope. Historical passed milestones remain historical: later planned edits are reviewed by subsequent milestones and the final checkpoint. A final checkpoint's persisted PASS is not fresh evidence after restart or subsequent writes until verify recomputes current hashes.

Rechecking a previously passed non-final milestone may report that its snapshot is no longer current, but must not erase its historical barrier success or automatically reopen it. Final PASS and sealed-run completion are distinct: an ordinary verify call does not prevent bounded corrective work before an explicit successful final complete request.

The product XML extension is an optional execution section with mode inline, classic, or delegated. Delegated execution contains review_checkpoints with unique CHECKPOINT-R-NNN elements. Each checkpoint has kind milestone or final, after_wave referencing WAVE-N, covers/task_id references, scope/file entries, reviewers/reviewer entries, acceptance/criterion entries, and verification/command entries. Task write_scope/file lists are required for delegated plans and include each task's primary file.

For delegated plans, enforce exactly one final checkpoint after the last wave, complete final task coverage, and scope coverage of all declared task write scopes. Milestones cannot cover future-wave tasks. The existing component, wave, and task identities remain unchanged. Legacy plans without execution retain their meaning; adding a new execution policy to an approved legacy plan needs explicit amendment.

Extend the existing spec-lint engine with typed extractDelegatedPlanDefinition output so runtime registration and validation share one contract rather than separate XML interpretations. The I/O adapter loads actual sibling files and runs cross-file validation; the linter itself remains filesystem-free. Increment LINT_VERSION so cached old verdicts cannot validate new policy silently.

Persist version 2 with legacy work-item records, delegated attempt/decision records, and plan-run/checkpoint data. Read valid version 1 conservatively with an empty plan-run registry. Keep the existing nullable hydration helper for compatibility, but provide a checked loader for the plugin to distinguish missing data from invalid new state rather than silently restarting an invalid run.

New controller mutations are staged and committed only after validation; checked persistence failures must be surfaced rather than acknowledged as durable acceptance. Keep legacy helper failure behavior compatible, use a bounded atomic temporary-file replacement for new snapshots, and avoid replacing an in-memory store reference across an await in a way that loses concurrent callback updates.

Bound control text to a non-empty rationale of at most 2000 characters and one to eight non-empty evidence references of at most 512 characters each; bound concerns disposition to 2000 characters. Evidence references are inert strings, not commands executed by workflow tooling. Preserve the existing 500-character recovery-excerpt policy for worker/reviewer output.

Managed execution vocabulary becomes inline, classic, and delegated. An explicit approved plan/user choice is reused when compatible with the active session policy; missing or conflicting intent is clarified before writes. This does not change the separately installed GRACE skill approval or mode-selection rules governing this implementation session.

Provider aliases use the exact approved model IDs, efforts, and limits. The fetched OpenCode config schema supports provider.models options, modalities, limits, and variants entries with disabled flags. Explicitly disable unsupported inherited Spark variants rather than treating variants: {} as disabling automatically generated variants. User-owned agent overrides are not clobbered.

Only repair.ts control-tool denial entries and /context native-tool attribution change outside the core new path. They are required integrations of the new tools, not a broader repair, Guardian, TUI, or role-system redesign. New helper files get their own module contracts and three new graph owners.

All listed scopes are literal file paths. Durable reconciliation is centralized in T-011 after observed behavior verifies. The package version, changelog, release scripts, installed config, global skills, and archived changes are outside implementation write scope. Approved plan assertions/scopes/tasks are never refreshed in place during execution.

One final independent review round is scheduled after the feature and its evidence are complete. Fix confirmed findings directly within the approved scope and rerun relevant gates. A materially new scope or contradicted contract requires rerouting, not speculative expansion of this plan.

The user-authorized implementation commit is made after final verification and diff review, without a push or release. Explicit GRACE apply confirmation is still required before marking documents applied and archiving; do not equate a Git commit with lifecycle apply.

T-003.Title: Add conservative file-scope normalization and deterministic snapshot fingerprints.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create src/plugins/workflow/snapshots.ts and snapshots.test.ts under M-WORKFLOW-SNAPSHOTS. Export a pure scope normalizer and captureWorkflowSnapshot using the trusted workspace root and explicit file paths.

Canonical hashing is order-independent for equivalent declarations and changes for content edits, creation, deletion, relevant mode changes, or a changed covered acceptance attempt. It does not change solely for mtime changes or unrelated files.

Reject traversal, absolute/wildcard inputs, duplicate path aliases, symlinks including ancestor symlinks, unsupported filesystem entries, root mismatch, unreadable files, and observed concurrent reads that cannot yield a coherent fingerprint. Represent absent paths explicitly and stream regular file content.

No commands or network calls are made and no source or snapshot-copy directories are created. Tests use isolated temporary roots and actual filesystem mutations. Covers snapshot portions of AC-10, AC-11, AC-13, and AC-29.

T-004.Title: Implement delegated work-item attempts and explicit controller decisions.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create delegated.ts and delegated.test.ts under M-WORKFLOW-DELEGATED. Extend state.ts and transitions.ts additively with mode delegated, awaiting_acceptance, declared write scope, optional plan binding, a host-call-bound attempt ledger, and controller decision history.

Only explicit delegated mode accepts requiredReviewers: []; the old modes keep non-empty reviewer requirements. A standalone delegated task does not require a plan package. Invalid mixed fields and legacy/new intent mismatches fail before mutation.

At launch allocate attempt one or two and bind callID; block another in-flight implementation. Apply only a matching completed call's result. DONE waits for acceptance; DONE_WITH_CONCERNS retains its status and bounded excerpt; hard stops remain hard stops. Malformed completed delegated output never yields acceptance and requires explicit recovery if bounded format repair fails.

Implement decideDelegatedWorkItem: accept records evidence and reaches ready_to_close, request_changes returns the first completed attempt to implementation, and exhaustion blocks further automatic attempts. Validate attempt, state, evidence bounds, and concerns disposition; reject duplicates and wrong-mode decisions without mutation.

Define a guarded rework reducer preserving prior acceptance history and consumed attempts. The caller must supply validated checkpoint-failure authorization before reopening an accepted delegated item; blocked/needs_context records cannot be reopened. Legacy review counters, close logic, and result headers are unchanged. Covers AC-05 through AC-09 and AC-29.

T-005.Title: Implement approved-plan registration and checkpoint state independently of review-only closure.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create checkpoints.ts, checkpoint-io.ts, and their tests under M-WORKFLOW-CHECKPOINTS. Extend WorkItemStoreData with an initialized plan-run registry. Keep domain transitions separate from approved-file loading and fingerprint I/O.

loadApprovedDelegatedPlan safely loads an active project-local vvoc plan and its linked approved spec, runs full cross-file lint, extracts typed obligations, and records canonical paths, workspace, and content hashes. Reject archives, unresolved or escaping refs, non-approved inputs, and incompatible modes.

registerDelegatedPlan stages and atomically registers all declared tasks and checkpoints without launching agents. Bind unique canonical task IDs to stable delegated work-item IDs; identical registration is idempotent, while changed plan/spec hashes or conflicting definitions produce explicit drift errors without resetting progress.

Starting a due checkpoint requires the declared wave's prerequisite tasks and covered attempts to be accepted, captures a fresh fingerprint, and opens the exact declared reviewer set through a new linked review_only work item. Bind review work item, generation, and reviewer call identities to that checkpoint.

Derive checkpoint outcome from linked recorded reviewer statuses and fresh fingerprint comparison, never from work-item closure or a supplied PASS flag. Retain historical milestones even when their old snapshots are no longer current; require their historical barrier success before dependent-wave launches. Final complete: true requires complete latest task/attempt/scope coverage and seals the run only after fresh verification.

Reject overlapping declared writes during in-flight review. Allow one checkpoint correction/review retry without resetting attempt histories. Authorize rework only for a covered accepted task in the same unfinished run after a settled failed checkpoint; a hard stop cannot authorize rework. Exhaustion requires explicit recovery.

Tests cover partial registration rollback, unknown refs, missing prerequisites, skipped checkpoint attempts, FAIL then close, review-only NEEDS_CONTEXT, old-generation callbacks, edits between start/result/verify, preserved historical milestones, final drift after restart, and plan/spec mutation. Covers AC-10 through AC-13, AC-17, and AC-29.

Validate new mode-specific fields, attempt sequencing and budgets, actor-independent stored decision shapes, task bindings, review generations, checkpoint links, cross-session/root mismatches, and historical versus current approval state. Reject missing or contradictory new data.

Keep the existing nullable hydration API compatible and add a checked loader/snapshot path for runtime integration that distinguishes missing, valid, and invalid state and surfaces I/O failures. Do not silently reset a malformed version 2 run to an empty valid run.

Round-trip accepted tasks, reworked histories, incomplete reviews, FAIL reports, passed historical milestones, final fingerprints, hard stops, and bounded excerpts. A persisted PASS still requires a fresh final snapshot check. Original persistence scenarios in workflow.test.ts pass. Covers AC-20 and persistence portions of AC-06 through AC-13.

Integrate checked persistence so failed new control transactions are not returned as durable success. Use staged fresh state and synchronous commit boundaries without dropping intervening updates. Preserve legacy tool behavior and generic review_only FAIL semantics.

Add the two tool IDs to repair.ts's disabled-tool map and /context's VVOC_TOOL_IDS. Update source-local contracts/maps/summaries and focused attribution tests; make no broader tool-policy or TUI changes.

T-012.Title: Run final evidence, obtain one independent review round, and create the authorized implementation commit.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Run the selected target assertion check and the selected final GRACE assertion gate externally; the final gate's --run-commands supplies fresh evidence for all target leaf commands without a redundant manual duplicate. Resolve or obtain explicit disposition of the recorded navigation/module-health problem before execution; do not waive any new lint/assertion/test failure.

Open one review_only work item with required spec and code reviewers for the completed change. Collect the complete round, personally validate findings, fix confirmed issues directly within the approved scope, and rerun fresh relevant gates. Hard-stop results are surfaced rather than retried automatically.

Before committing, inspect git status, the full intended diff, and git log --oneline -10. Stage only intended approved-scope files, exclude credentials/generated output/unrelated user changes, and create the user-authorized conventional implementation commit. Do not push, release, skip hooks, or amend a failed commit.

Report the commit and criterion-level outcome with remaining live-model/performance limits. Request explicit GRACE apply confirmation after fresh end-state evidence; keep the bundle active and approved until that confirmation rather than marking it applied or archiving it autonomously. Covers AC-30 and the approved verification intent.
